themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street Condition complaints exploded to 127 this week vs. a baseline of 18.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 582% spike (z-score: 13.77)—suggesting rapid pavement failure or construction disruption affecting Park Slope and Carroll Gardens residents this week.
evidence: 127 Street Condition complaints last week vs. 18.6 weekly average (582% increase, z-score 13.77)
Highest z-score spike in the dataset, indicating strongest statistical anomaly
CB budget requests show repeated year-over-year asks for street/infrastructure repair, suggesting chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Map the 127 complaints geographically—are they clustered on specific blocks or corridors?
Interview DOT about whether this is weather-related (winter damage), construction-related, or deferred maintenance catching up

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged Tree complaints spiked to 16 this week from a baseline of 2.4 per week—a 574% increase (z-score: 11.18)—marking the second-highest statistical anomaly and suggesting either a recent storm, pest outbreak, or infrastructure conflict affecting the neighborhood's canopy this week.
evidence: 16 Damaged Tree complaints this week vs. 2.4 weekly average (574% increase, z-score 11.18)
Chronic CB budget request to 'Reconstruct or upgrade a building in a park' and park safety—suggests trees may be infrastructure liability
reporting_angles: Was there a weather event (high winds, ice storm) this week that triggered complaints?
Are tree deaths concentrated in specific parks (Prospect Park, Carroll Park) or street segments, and are they related to street/sewer work?

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints jumped to 19 this week from a baseline of 4.8 per week—a 300% spike (z-score: 6.76)—coinciding with the Street Condition surge and suggesting possible underground infrastructure compromise affecting Park Slope/Carroll Gardens this week.
evidence: 19 Sewer complaints this week vs. 4.8 weekly average (300% increase, z-score 6.76)
Converges with Street Condition spike—both may point to shared underground cause (water main break, seasonal discharge)
CB budget requests repeatedly ask for 'Inspect water main on specific street segment and repair or replace as needed' (Agency: DEP)
reporting_angles: Did DEP experience a water main break or emergency discharge this week? Cross-check with local incident reports.
Interview residents on affected blocks: are they experiencing basement flooding, backed-up sewage, or odors?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping & Sanitation Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Dumping (220% spike: 26 complaints last week vs. 8.1 avg, z-score 6.95) and Dirty Condition (260% spike: 63 complaints last week vs. 17.5 avg, z-score 6.28) surged in tandem over the past week, suggesting a sanitation services failure or organized dumping activity in the district.
evidence: 26 Illegal Dumping complaints last week vs. 8.1 weekly baseline (220% increase, z-score 6.95)
63 Dirty Condition complaints last week vs. 17.5 weekly baseline (260% increase, z-score 6.28)
Two-issue spike suggests systemic sanitation problem rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Are DSNY collection schedules disrupted or reduced? Check with Sanitation union and agency.
Canvass neighborhoods to identify dumping hotspots and interview residents—is this organized debris from construction sites or street-level abandonment?

themes_detail.label: Noise Disturbances Rising
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints jumped to 33 last week from a baseline of 11.2 per week—a 193% increase (z-score: 6.65)—suggesting construction, transit disruption, or street-level activity escalation in the neighborhood over the past week.
evidence: 33 Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints last week vs. 11.2 weekly baseline (193% increase, z-score 6.65)
1001 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (638 Alterations, 105 New Buildings)—likely construction noise source
Multiple active ULURP/land use projects (46 Nelson Street Rezoning, GSD certifications) may signal equipment/demolition activity
reporting_angles: Cross-reference noise complaint locations with active DOB permits—are complaints clustered near major construction sites?
Interview CB about construction compliance and noise variance abuse.
